text:
maria: FYI I'm seeing a parity bug in the Node sampleapp when using the embeddings -> rerank pipeline under bursty traffic. Node SDK batching helper (v0.8.1) sometimes returns an embeddings array that cannot be mapped back to the candidate IDs by index. Repro on dev pretty reliable.

jamal: Can you share a minimal repro and logs? Are vectors missing or did indices move around?

maria: Minimal repro: send this payload of 4 candidates:
```json
{"candidates": [{"id":"a1","text":"alpha"},{"id":"b2","text":"beta"},{"id":"c3","text":"gamma"},{"id":"d4","text":"delta"}]}
```
When the batcher retries an auth error we sometimes end up with embeddings like [vec_b2, vec_a1, vec_d4, vec_c3] (same 4 vectors but shuffled). The server rerank expects positional ordering so results are wrong.

elaine: Do we send any per-input identifier with the request today? I thought embeddings were position-only.

maria: Correct, current API returns just an array of vectors. No echoed ids. Node helper tries to be memory-efficient: it trims null placeholders on partial responses and concatenates chunks. Under concurrent retries the chunk merge order can change. Logs:
```
[2026-03-20T09:12:01Z] batcher send batch id=bt-91 size=4
[2026-03-20T09:12:01Z] runtime: 401 unauthorized token=rot-44
[2026-03-20T09:12:01Z] batcher: retrying batch id=bt-91 with placeholders
[2026-03-20T09:12:02Z] batcher: received chunk size=3 chunk_idx=1
[2026-03-20T09:12:02Z] batcher: received chunk size=1 chunk_idx=0
[2026-03-20T09:12:02Z] batcher: merge -> final len=4 order=[1,0,3,2]
```

noah: That merge ordering is the issue. Python SDK's batcher preserves an explicit index map so it never reorders. Node's helper uses positional assumptions for speed.

toni: Two levels of fixes: 1) short-term SDK patch to attach ephemeral client_input_ids to each request element and reindex by those IDs on response merge; 2) longer-term API change to make embeddings return [{input_id, embedding}] objects or echo back input ids.

jamal: For backward compatibility we can add optional echoing: server returns `input_ids` alongside the embeddings array when header `X-Echo-Input-Ids: true` is present. That way SDKs can switch without breaking older clients. We should document this in the SDK changelog and draft a small RFC for making it standard.

maria: Short-term workaround for customers: pin to Python SDK or set Node SDK retry to 0, or upgrade to the hotfix branch. We need a hotfix in Node SDK sampleapp because customers often copy it verbatim.

noah: I'll prototype the Node fix: generate a uuid per candidate (client_input_id) and attach it to the outgoing request metadata. On merging partial responses, map by client_input_id instead of by index. Low-risk and fully backward compatible.

elaine: From runtime side, we can add quick support to echo `client_input_id` if present in the request. That requires small change to the embeddings handler to accept and echo that field. ops-bot: note deploy needed but low blast radius.

ops-bot: Acknowledged. staging test and a short deploy window required. No DB migrations.

jamal: I'll open a GH issue: "node-sdk: batcher must preserve per-input ids and merge partial responses deterministically" and tag node + devex + backport.

toni: Tests I will add: fuzz the batcher by shuffling chunk delivery orders, simulating 401/5xx partials, and assert output mapping by client_input_id equals expected mapping. Will add to node-sdk CI and sampleapp integration tests.

maria: Also add a small integration test in retriever that maps embeddings by id (once we support echoing). That will catch regressions if some SDKs don't upgrade.

noah: Pushed a WIP PR branch `fix/batcher-id-map` with the client_input_id approach and added a manual test script.

jamal: Created issue and linked the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/issues/432 (label: bug, priority: high, backport: v0.8.x).

maria: Thanks. I'll coordinate an RFC to standardize the non-breaking echo and timeline for making it mandatory. For now, action items: noah - finish patch + tests, jamal - backport issue, elaine - runtime echo support behind header, toni - CI fuzz tests, maria - integration test for retriever.

noah: Hotfix merged to `hotfix/embed-echo` and deployed to dev. Verified with 50k requests under jittered auth rotations: no misaligned pairs.

maria: Verified on dev too. Great work. We'll schedule the RFC review next week. :thumbsup:
